title: Prions: Infection Without a Living Germ
hook: Chronic wasting disease can spread silently from deer that look perfectly healthy — a reminder that some infections are caused not by a microbe, but by a misshapen protein.
key_points: Prions are misfolded proteins that force normal copies to misfold too — no DNA or cells involved.
A new study found infectious prions in chronic-wasting-disease deer showing no symptoms.
That means the disease can spread silently, before any signs appear.
Researchers warn the prion can evolve and jump between species.
There is no confirmed risk to humans, but they urge close monitoring.
content_html: Most infections come from a living invader — a bacterium or a virus carrying its own genetic code. Prions break that rule. A prion is simply a normal body protein that has folded into the wrong shape, and its only "trick" is to bump into healthy copies of the same protein and force them to misfold as well. The damage spreads in a chain reaction, with no DNA, no cells, and nothing alive involved. Prion diseases like chronic wasting disease (CWD) in deer are untreatable and invariably fatal.
extra_html: A new study, reported via ScienceDaily, adds a worrying wrinkle: infectious prions turned up in CWD-infected deer that showed no symptoms at all. That means the disease can spread silently, passing between animals long before anyone could spot a sick one. The researchers also caution that the prion can evolve and cross between species. They stress there is no confirmed risk to humans — but given how relentlessly prions behave, they argue the disease deserves close monitoring rather than complacency.

related.title: How Infections Spread
related.hook: Germs can't fly to a new host on their own — they hitch rides on coughs, hands, food, water, and insects. Break the ride, and you break the chain of infection.

related.title: Are Viruses Alive?
related.hook: A virus is little more than genes in a protein shell — it can't eat, grow, or reproduce on its own, which is why biologists still argue whether it counts as living.

flashcards.prompt: What is a prion, and how does it differ from a virus or bacterium?
flashcards.back_html: A prion is a misfolded protein that forces normal proteins to misfold too. It has no DNA, RNA, or cells — it isn't a living germ at all, yet it spreads disease.

flashcards.prompt: Why is the finding that infected deer can look healthy concerning?

choices.text: The disease can spread silently before any symptoms show
It means the deer have recovered on their own
It proves the disease can't infect other animals

flashcards.explanation_html: Infectious prions were present in deer with no symptoms, so chronic wasting disease can pass to others before anyone can tell an animal is sick.

flashcards.prompt: What did researchers say about the risk to people?

choices.text: No confirmed human risk, but the cross-species threat warrants close watching
Prions can never cross between species

flashcards.explanation_html: There is no confirmed human risk so far, but because the prion can evolve and jump species, the researchers call for careful monitoring rather than complacency.
